basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 19.' and it opens '(Vers. 19.) Et foderunt pueri Isaac in valle Gerarum, et invenerunt ibi puteum aquae'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 19.) Et foderunt pueri Isaac in valle Gerarum, et invenerunt ibi puteum aquae vivae. Et hic pro valle, torrens scriptus est; numquam enim in valle invenitur puteus aquae vivae.
